articles.title: Five New Google Flow Tools Designed by Visual Artists
articles.summary: Five new tools land in Google Flow, the AI creative studio, each built by a working artist or filmmaker. Character Poster and Character Arc keep characters consistent in style and across ages, while Pixel Machine adds bitmap, ASCII, CRT, and glitch looks. Lucid Glass simulates prisms and refractions no real lens can capture, and Pocket Studio turns a single phone take into multiple polished camera angles.

articles.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Hydrogen with ‘significant leaps' in speed, intelligence
articles.summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing the Flash branding with a model designed to deliver higher intelligence and faster performance at an accessible price. Compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen reportedly completes tasks 2.5 times faster at its default high setting, more than triples its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score, and reduces fabricated claims by over fivefold. It also supports a native one-million-token input and output context, with improvements in tool recovery, multimodal reasoning, and complex agentic workflows.

articles.title: Adobe's AI Experiments Let You Walk Around in Photos and Interview Your Characters
articles.summary: Adobe's experimental “sneaks” at its Max conference include AI tools that turn photos into explorable 3D scenes, let users interview characters, and make edits copy-pasteable. Screen Test shapes AI characters' personalities through conversation, while Sight Span turns flat images into navigable 3D spaces. Sound Bender generates cursor-adjustable audio and Rinse Repeat copies Photoshop edits to other subjects, though these tech previews may never become Creative Cloud or Firefly features.

articles.title: Design is a Search Problem
articles.summary: Design is a search problem: finding the right solution in a vast space of possibilities, which computer science's search algorithms help explain. Beam search mirrors the "show me some options" approach that AI has made far wider, while A* matches a more deliberate process steered by a good heuristic. AI has widened the beam without improving the heuristic, so empathy and taste remain the human edge.

articles.title: Every click has a price now. Who designs how that “feels”?
articles.summary: As AI products shift toward credit- and usage-based pricing, everyday interactions increasingly carry a visible financial cost, creating new challenges for user experience design. Unpredictable charges, unclear token consumption, and sudden usage limits can undermine trust, making transparent cost estimates, spending controls, and understandable feedback essential interface features. Designers must also decide when expensive AI processing is justified and when simpler alternatives can deliver the same result without introducing unnecessary cost or anxiety.

articles.title: Build Faster Without Leaving Accessibility Behind
articles.summary: The newly open-sourced Accessibility Considerations Toolkit (ACT) helps teams find barriers before AI-assisted development repeats the same mistakes across more interfaces, faster. It pairs access strategies and assistive technologies with usability heuristics and standards references, in Markdown for people and YAML for agents and pipelines. ACT doesn't replace testing with disabled people or establish compliance, and its findings still need human review.

articles.title: Protect Human Writing by Poisoning Unauthorized AI Training (Website)
articles.summary: Publish for humans, not for crawlers. A web font that swaps the words in your HTML, so readers see your writing and scrapers get a decoy copy.

articles.title: Neumorphism CSS Generator (Website)
articles.summary: Easily generate soft UI and Neumorphism CSS styles. Customize colors and shadows, then copy the code.

articles.title: Everything You've Saved, in One Visual Library (Website)
articles.summary: One visual library for everything you save on Instagram, X, TikTok, Pinterest, and more. Tagged by AI, searchable by meaning and color, and kept even when the post is gone.

articles.title: Circuit: Civic Shuttle Brand Identity by The Collected Works
articles.summary: The Collected Works has redesigned Circuit, an electric shuttle service operating across 50 cities, to replace its fragmented local identities with a cohesive brand inspired by dependable public infrastructure. The refreshed system retains Circuit's original C symbol, introduces Stadt and Haffer typography, and uses directional arrows, road-inspired graphics, and a restrained green palette to evoke urban transportation. A custom generative tool creates continuous route-like graphics, while standardized fleet wraps and flexible local messaging help the identity remain consistent across different cities.

articles.title: Bruno's HelloAsso identity follows France's love of brands with values
articles.summary: Bruno has rebranded HelloAsso, a free platform serving 480,000 French nonprofits, with a new identity built around the idea of individuals coming together to form a collective. Its central graphic device is a mosaic of real member portraits, where individual squares can split to accommodate text, supported by bold Franklin Gothic typography, candid photography, and an expressive color palette. The system extends across HelloAsso Sport, Generosity, Culture, and its Fund for Engagement, giving each offering a distinctive visual personality while maintaining a recognizable shared identity.

articles.title: Japanese Logos: 43 Classic Logo Designs and the Stories Behind Them
articles.summary: Japanese graphic design produced some of the world's most influential corporate identities between the 1960s and early 1990s, with designers including Yusaku Kamekura, Ikko Tanaka, Kazumasa Nagai, and Takenobu Igarashi. Forty-three classic logos spanning Sony, NTT, Japan Airlines, Mazda, and the Tokyo 1964 Olympics demonstrate how modernist geometry, cultural symbolism, and distinctive visual ideas helped establish recognizable identities. Many also emerged from strategic corporate identity programs, particularly those developed by PAOS, that connected visual design with broader organizational transformation.

articles.title: Band-Aid Accessibility
articles.summary: More disabled people are using LLM coding tools to build the accessible features and apps mainstream software never delivered.

articles.title: Brand Insistence: Why the Strongest Brands Have No Substitutes
articles.summary: The strongest brands push customers past preference and loyalty to insistence, where they'll wait, search, or pay more because there's no substitute.

articles.title: The toy company Tomy has a new logo, and people are baffled
articles.summary: Japanese toymaker Tomy is adopting the unified global name Takara Tomy and replacing its familiar blue-and-white logo with a new identity featuring a teal-to-magenta gradient symbol inspired by the Japanese characters for "asobi" (play).
